name: pars-optimizer
author: Pars Host Developer Team

sections.description:
Crafted with 💙 by the programmers and developers at Pars.host, pars-optimizer is programmed to significantly enhance your website’s load speed, ensuring a seamless and faster user experience. Say goodbye to slow loading times!

pars-optimizer is not just a speed plugin; it’s a complete toolkit for WordPress efficiency. It combines security features, performance optimizations, and UI enhancements in one lightweight package.

Key Features:

🚀 Performance & Speed
* Minify CSS & JS: Compress your style and script files to reduce size.
* Merge Assets: Combine multiple CSS/JS files into one to reduce HTTP requests.
* Lazy Load: Built-in lazy loading for Images and Iframes to speed up initial page load.
* Remove Comments: Automatically strips HTML comments from your source code.
* Preload Resources: Easily define critical assets (fonts, CSS, JS) to preload for better Core Web Vitals.

🛡️ Security Enhancements
* Hide Login URL: Change your default wp-admin and wp-login.php to a custom slug (e.g., /my-login) to prevent brute-force attacks.
* Force SSL: Enforce HTTPS redirection for both the admin dashboard and the frontend.

🛒 WooCommerce Optimization
* Disable Tracking: Stop WooCommerce from tracking usage data to speed up your backend.

🎨 Admin Interface & Fonts
* Persian Font (Yekan Bakh): Beautiful “Yekan Bakh” font integration for both the Admin Dashboard and Frontend.
* Modern Admin Theme: A sleek, dark/modern theme for the WordPress dashboard to improve the management experience.

🌍 Fully Translatable
* Every string in the interface is translatable, and a complete Persian (fa_IR) translation ships with the plugin.
* The admin screens are built with CSS logical properties, so the whole interface mirrors correctly for right-to-left languages.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to the /wp-content/plugins/pars-optimo directory, or install the plugin through the WordPress plugins screen directly.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ screen in WordPress.
  3. Use the Optimizer menu to configure the settings.
  4. Go to the Analysis tab to check your website’s optimization score.
sections.faq:
Does this plugin work with other caching plugins?

Yes, pars-optimizer is designed to be lightweight and compatible. However, if you use another plugin for Minify/Merge functionality (like Autoptimize), we recommend disabling those specific features in one of the plugins to avoid conflicts.

How do I change my login URL?

Go to Optimizer > Settings > Security. Enable “Hide Login URL”, enter your desired slug (e.g., secret-login), and save. Important: If you get a 404 error, go to Settings > Permalinks and just click “Save Changes” to flush the rewrite rules.

What if I get locked out after changing the login URL?

Simply rename the pars-optimo folder in wp-content/plugins/ via FTP or File Manager to deactivate the plugin. Then you can access wp-login.php again.

Is the plugin available in Persian?

Yes. A complete Persian (fa_IR) translation is bundled. Set your site language to فارسی under Settings > General and the whole interface switches over, including right-to-left layout.

How can I translate the plugin into my own language?

A languages/pars-optimo.pot template is included. You can also translate the plugin on translate.wordpress.org, and the resulting language pack will be picked up automatically.
sections.changelog:
1.1.1

  • Fixed: Text rendered a full weight heavier than intended everywhere the Yekan Bakh font was active. The bundled @font-face block mapped font-weight: 400 — normal body text — to the SemiBold file, and 700 to ExtraBold, so there was no way for any stylesheet to ask for true Regular. Weights are now mapped to the files they actually belong to (400 = Regular, 600 = SemiBold, 700 = Bold).
  • Fixed: The font stylesheet also applied global typography of its own: body and h1–h6 had their font family forced with !important, every heading was pinned to font-weight: 700, and h1–h6 were given fixed pixel sizes (40px/32px/24px/18px/16px/14px). Simply enabling the font therefore overrode the heading scale of the active theme and of the WordPress dashboard. The file now only registers the family; applying it is handled by the stylesheets tied to each option.
  • Fixed: woff was listed before woff2 in every @font-face, so modern browsers downloaded the larger file. woff2 now comes first.
  • Fixed: The ExtraBold @font-face pointed its woff2 source at the .woff file.
  • Changed: The admin interface now uses a deliberate type scale — six whole-pixel sizes and only two weights (Regular for text, SemiBold for emphasis), with hierarchy carried by size and colour rather than heavy weights.
  • Changed: Persian typography is handled separately from Latin: more line height, no letter-spacing (which breaks the joined baseline of Arabic-script text), and the webfont leads the stack only in right-to-left locales so Latin interfaces keep the system font.
  • Changed: Counters and scores use tabular figures so numbers no longer shift their neighbours as they change.

1.1.0

  • Fixed: “Remove HTML Comments” used an invalid regular expression that made preg_replace() return NULL, which served a completely blank page on the front end. The pattern is rewritten (IE conditional comments are now preserved) and every buffered replacement falls back to the original markup if a match ever fails.
  • Fixed: The Yekan Bakh font options had no effect. The bundled @font-face registers the family as yekan-bakh, but the stylesheet asked for Yekan Bakh. The font now applies on both the dashboard and the front end, and the two options work independently of the admin theme.
  • Fixed: The deactivation routine was registered with register_activation_hook(), so it ran on activation and never on deactivation.
  • Fixed: Default options written at activation used a lazy_load key that no longer exists, instead of lazy_load_images / lazy_load_iframe.
  • Added: Full internationalization. Every interface string now runs through the translation API, with a bundled Persian (fa_IR) translation and a .pot template.
  • Added: Text domain corrected to pars-optimo so it matches the plugin slug — language packs from translate.wordpress.org can now load.
  • Added: Redesigned admin interface — sidebar navigation with live per-section counters, a settings search filter, a sticky save bar with unsaved-change warnings, deep-linkable tabs, and an overview screen with scores and actionable next steps.
  • Added: Right-to-left support throughout, implemented with CSS logical properties so there is no separate RTL stylesheet.
  • Added: Keyboard-accessible tabs with proper ARIA roles, visible focus styles, and prefers-reduced-motion support.
  • Added: “Settings” shortcut link on the Plugins screen, and a confirmation notice after saving.
  • Added: The Analysis screen now explains each failed check and links straight to the setting that resolves it.
  • Changed: Settings are now declared in a single schema that drives the interface, the counters and validation, so the three can no longer drift apart.
  • Changed: Removed an unprefixed global return_no() function from the global namespace.

1.0.0

  • Initial release.
  • Added Security features (Hide Login, Force SSL).
  • Added Optimization features (Minify, Merge, Lazy Load).
  • Added WooCommerce optimization.
  • Added Admin Theme and Custom Fonts.
